items.title: By-eye look: the course procedure's what-you-should-see column
Method choice changes which lesions are shown and how many

effect.text: Method choice changes which lesions are shown and how many: on serial sections of two AD brains, a modified Bielschowsky stain demonstrated more tangles, and more distinctly, than the Bodian stain (Yamamoto and Hirano 1986). No source in the registry compares Bielschowsky with CPS on the same sections.

items.title: Silver methods differ in sensitivity and most lack control in some steps

effect.text: Among six silver methods compared on hippocampal serial sections, Gallyas and Bielschowsky were among the most sensitive for tangles, and the authors state that most silver methods are not reliable because certain steps lack control (Rosenwald et al. 1993).

items.system: hippocampal serial sections, 35 human brains, paraffin

items.title: CPS-I schematic outcome (Velasco 1992)

effect.text: Compare-only method; not runnable on the bench; schematic from the published description.
In CPS-I the dystrophic neurites of plaques are obscured by amyloid argyrophilia (Velasco 1992); the schematic shows the plaque stained as a whole and cannot show the neurites separately.

items.title: CPS-II schematic outcome (Velasco 1992)

effect.text: Compare-only method; not runnable on the bench; schematic from the published description.

Axon 0 and plaque core 1 (trace) are schematic readings of the CPS-II description: the abstract states unstained normal neurites for CPS-I, not CPS-II, and says amyloid staining is suppressed, not abolished.

items.title: Developer strength: too weak gives light, incomplete staining; too strong loses differentiation

effect.text: In nerve tissue sections, developers that were too weak gave light, incomplete staining and developers that were too strong gave no differentiated nerve staining (Peters 1955). The course procedure's developer (3 drops of a formaldehyde, citric acid and nitric acid stock per 50 ml of ammoniacal silver, judged under the microscope) is not characterized on those axes here; the strength positions weak / sop-default / strong are ordered schematic positions only.

items.title: Binding and metallic-silver formation are separable processes with different time courses

effect.text: Binding of silver ions and formation of metallic silver are separable processes with different time courses (Gallyas 1979). The curves are schematic shapes only: not calibrated to any tissue, and the course Gallyas activity concerns treated human spinal cord, whose data were not consulted. A plateau in binding does not mean visible deposition has finished.

items.system: schematic shapes; Gallyas papers verified by title only

items.title: Intensity tracks site chemistry, not protein amount alone

effect.text: In polyacrylamide gels, ammoniacal silver staining intensity was directly related to the lysine content of standard proteins, and the authors proposed that deposition builds on nucleation sites formed before the developer is added (Dion and Pomenti 1983). This is a different system: an analogy for why intensity is not a direct measure of protein amount, never a calibration for brain tissue.

items.title: The same lesions are assessed differently across laboratories

effect.text: The same AD-related lesions received different assessments across laboratories (Alafuzoff et al. 2006), which motivates controls, matched sections and blinded scoring.

items.system: human brain, multiple laboratories (title and metadata only)

items.title: Protocol deviation: a step out of procedure order or repeated

effect.text: Protocol deviation: at least one step was performed out of the course procedure order or repeated. The illustrative state is whatever the performed order produced; no source in the registry describes the staining consequence of this deviation, so nothing beyond the recorded deviation is encoded.

items.title: A negative biological comparison still stains normal structures

effect.text: A negative biological comparison is not expected to be blank: normal neural structures such as axons can stain.

note: No R-hyp-* rules in v1. The course raises four competing explanations (C-course-hypotheses) but no source in the registry states which pretreatment probes which hypothesis or which direction each hypothesis predicts; filling that in from general chemistry would assert a hypothesis as true. Any pretreatment other than none resolves to an uncertainty card (hypothesis-unencoded). Any R-hyp-* rule added later must carry conditionalOn (lint hypothesis-rule-without-condition) and cite instructor guidance.
